findings.evidence: `pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1564` adds `ast.NullEQ` to the prunable operators. When the predicate is written as `const <=> col`, `extractDataForPrune` swaps operands via `ret.op = opposite(ret.op)` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1583-1587`, also `:1594-1599` for CAST). But `opposite()` (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:1708-1721`) has no `ast.NullEQ` case and panics on unknown ops. Same pattern exists in RANGE COLUMNS pruning: `rangeColumnsPruner.partitionRangeForExpr` calls `opName = opposite(opName)` when the column is on the right (`pkg/planner/core/rule_partition_processor.go:2063-2067`, also `:2074-2079`). Second confirmation (different evidence): expression rewriting preserves operand order (no canonical swap) when building `NullEQ`: `binaryOpToExpression` calls `constructBinaryOpFunction(lhs, rhs, op)` (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:1787-1794`), and the base case emits `newFunction(op, ..., l, r)` unchanged (`pkg/planner/core/expression_rewriter.go:401-405`), so user SQL like `'D' <=> a` will indeed produce `nulleq(constant, column)` and hit the swap path.
findings.fix: Treat `ast.NullEQ` as symmetric in the swap logic: either add `case ast.NullEQ: return ast.NullEQ` to `opposite()`, or special-case callers to skip `opposite()` when `op==ast.NullEQ` (both in RANGE and RANGE COLUMNS pruners).
findings.impact: A user can trigger a planner panic (potential server crash/DoS or at least statement failure, depending on panic recovery) with queries that put the constant on the left of `<=>` against a RANGE / RANGE COLUMNS partitioning column, e.g. `SELECT ... FROM t WHERE 'D' <=> a` or `NULL <=> a`. This is a correctness/availability regression introduced by accepting `ast.NullEQ` without updating `opposite()`.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed up to `upstream/master` (`3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`): `pkg/planner/core/rule/rule_partition_processor.go` still allows `ast.NullEQ` and still executes `ret.Op = opposite(ret.Op)` on swapped args (`...:1604` in the upstream/master view), while `opposite()` still lacks a `ast.NullEQ` case and panics (`...:1681-1694` in the upstream/master view).
findings.verify: Add planner tests that exercise constant-left `<=>` forms on partitioned tables, e.g. `explain ... where 'D' <=> a` and `explain ... where NULL <=> a`, for both `PARTITION BY RANGE` and `PARTITION BY RANGE COLUMNS`. Verify no panic and that pruning matches the existing constant-right behavior.
findings.what: Partition pruning can panic on `const <=> col` (NullEQ) because operand-swapping calls `opposite()` with `ast.NullEQ`, but `opposite()` doesn’t handle `ast.NullEQ`.

subject: planner: Handle NullEQ <=> in range columns partition pruning (#61187)
summary: Adds `<=>` (NullEQ) support to RANGE / RANGE COLUMNS partition pruning by mapping non-NULL `<=>` to `=` and `NULL <=>` to `IS NULL`, plus regression tests for issue #61176. Introduces a new panic path when `<=>` is written with the constant on the left due to `opposite()` not handling `ast.NullEQ`.
